title: Cap. VI Arg. 7: from the absurdity — election suspended on human faith yields no fixed elect number
latin: Septimo, argumentamur ab inconveniente vel absurdo, quo laborat haec eorum sententia qui suspendunt actum electionis Divinae ex praeeunte actu fidei ac perseverantiae humanae. Hinc enim sequeretur, nec formalem nec materialem numerum electorum esse certum ac definitum secundum decretum aliquod beneplaciti Divini, sed quod hae singulares personae, et hoc definito numero, salventur, id per accidens evenisse, ex contingente nimirum actu arbitrii humani, Deo praevidente, non praeordinante.
pass_a: Seventhly, we argue from the inconvenience or absurdity under which this opinion of theirs labors who suspend the act of Divine election upon the preceding act of human faith and perseverance. For from this it would follow that neither the formal nor the material number of the elect is certain and defined according to some decree of Divine good pleasure, but that these singular persons, and in this defined number, are saved, happened by accident, namely from a contingent act of human choice, God foreseeing, not preordaining.
pass_b: Seventh argument: from the absurdity their view labors under — hanging divine election on a prior act of human faith and perseverance. Then neither the formal nor the material number of the elect would be fixed by any decree of divine good pleasure; that these particular persons are saved, and in this fixed count, would be an accident of contingent human choice — God foreseeing, not preordaining.

title: Cap. VI Arg. 7: ancient Semi-Pelagians owned the sequitur — Faustus on free choice
latin: Antiqui Semipelagiani viderunt hoc necessario sequi ex praedicta sententia, atque idcirco tanquam nihil absurdi in se haberet, hoc palam docuerunt. Sic Faustus De lib. arbit. lib. 1. Status hominis in diversa, non pro constitutione Dei, sed pro arbitrii libertate potest versari. Et libro 1. cap. 20. Quid de nobis praescire ac praeordinare debeat Deus, quantum pertinet ad futurum, in profectu hominis defectuque consistit.
pass_a: The ancient Semi-Pelagians saw that this necessarily follows from the aforesaid opinion, and therefore, as if it had nothing absurd in itself, taught this openly. So Faustus, On Free Choice, book 1: The state of man into diverse things can turn not according to the constitution of God, but according to the liberty of choice. And book 1, chapter 20: What God ought to foreknow and preordain concerning us, as far as pertains to the future, consists in the progress and defect of man.
pass_b: The old Semi-Pelagians saw that sequitur and taught it openly as no absurdity. Faustus (On Free Choice 1): a man's state can turn this way or that not by God's constitution but by free choice. And 1.20: what God is to foreknow and preordain about us for the future consists in man's progress or failure.

title: Cap. VI Arg. 7: Prosper and Hilary — Pelagian remnants reject a fixed elect number
latin: Multo autem apertius id asseruerunt Pelagianorum reliqui, apud Prosperum et Hilarium in Epistolis ad Augustinum. Sic igitur Prosper: Non acquiescunt praedestinationi, electorum numerum nec augeri posse nec minui. Et Hilarius: Hi non recipiunt, ut eligendorum et rejiciendorum esse definitum numerum velint.
pass_a: But much more openly did the remnants of the Pelagians assert this, in Prosper and Hilary in the Letters to Augustine. So therefore Prosper: They do not acquiesce in predestination, that the number of the elect can neither be increased nor diminished. And Hilary: These do not receive it, that they should will there to be a defined number of those to be elected and rejected.
pass_b: The Pelagian remnants said it more openly still — Prosper and Hilary in their letters to Augustine. Prosper: they will not grant predestination that the elect's number can neither grow nor shrink. Hilary: they will not have a defined number of those to be chosen and rejected.

lemmas.lemma: electorum numerum nec augeri nec minui
lemmas.gloss: elect number neither increased nor diminished

title: Cap. VI Arg. 7: Lessius — complete predestination rare in Scripture; hangs on perseverance
latin: Atque ex nuperis Jesuitis Lessius, qui magis aperte hanc causam egit, confidenter asserit, De completa praedestinatione nullam aut raram esse mentionem in Scripturis, quia haec non pendet ex nudo Dei beneplacito, sed ex perseverantia humana. Quinetiam docet, Intentionem Dei de numero salvandorum non fuisse absolutam ante praevisionem finis mundi.
pass_a: And among recent Jesuits Lessius, who more openly pleaded this cause, confidently asserts that of complete predestination there is no mention, or rare mention, in the Scriptures, because this does not hang from the bare good pleasure of God, but from human perseverance. Moreover he teaches that God's intention concerning the number of those to be saved was not absolute before the foresight of the end of the world.
pass_b: Among recent Jesuits, Lessius presses it more openly: Scripture barely mentions complete predestination, he says, because it hangs not on bare good pleasure but on human perseverance. He even teaches that God's intention for the number of the saved was not absolute before foresight of the world's end.

lemmas.gloss: Jesuit: complete predestination rare in Scripture

title: Cap. VI Arg. 7 close: then Peter no more ordained than Judas — fights Eph. 1:4 and Acts 13:48
latin: Haec si ita essent, nulla esset differentia inter electos et praeteritos ex Divina operatione, sed solummodo ex humana; nec Petrus a Deo magis ordinatus ad vitam aeternam fuisset quam Judas: sed quia credendo et perseverando satisfecit universali huic decreto, Quisquis perseveranter crediderit, salvus erit, Judas autem non satisfecit, ideo fuit hic in electorum numerum receptus, iste ab eodem numero exclusus. Sed haec omnia sunt plane absurda et cum Scripturis pugnantia, quae docent quosdam in Christo electos ante jacta mundi fundamenta, ut essent sancti et inculpati, Eph. i. 4. Quosdam prae aliis fide donatos, quia prae aliis fuerunt a Deo ex mera misericordia ad vitam ordinati; ut Matth. xi. 25, 26; Act. xiii. 48; Joh. vi. 37; et alibi passim.
pass_a: If these things were so, there would be no difference between the elect and the passed-by from Divine operation, but only from human; nor would Peter have been more ordained by God to eternal life than Judas: but because by believing and persevering he satisfied this universal decree, Whosoever shall have perseveringly believed shall be saved, but Judas did not satisfy, therefore this one was received into the number of the elect, that one excluded from the same number. But all these things are plainly absurd and fighting with the Scriptures, which teach that certain ones were elected in Christ before the foundations of the world were laid, that they might be holy and blameless, Eph. 1:4. That certain ones were gifted with faith before others, because before others they were ordained by God from mere mercy to life; as Matt. 11:25-26; Acts 13:48; John 6:37; and elsewhere throughout.
pass_b: If so, elect and passed-by would differ only by human operation, not divine — and Peter would be no more ordained by God to eternal life than Judas. Peter would enter the elect number only because he met the universal decree Whoever perseveringly believes shall be saved; Judas failed it and was shut out. Plainly absurd, and at war with Scripture: some elected in Christ before the world's foundation, to be holy and blameless (Eph. 1:4); some gifted with faith before others because before others God from mere mercy ordained them to life — Matt. 11:25-26; Acts 13:48; John 6:37; and throughout.

lemmas.gloss: Peter no more ordained than Judas
elect before foundation; ordained to life
